_comment: DogTag leaf-commitment spec v1 conformance vectors. Every value here was produced by calling the existing dogtag-standard-ts implementation (packages/dogtag-standard-ts/src) directly - none are hand-computed. field_p is the BN254 scalar field modulus. See specs/leaf-commitment.md (conformance clause): an implementation is conformant iff it reproduces every vector here. Every leafHashVectors[].value is the exact literal to pass back into {tag, value} to reproduce expected_hex/expected_dec, EXCEPT Bytes, whose value is lowercase hex (no 0x prefix) - decode with hexToBytes before constructing the scalar. redactedArtifactVectors (section 15, WP4.10S) exercises verifyRedactedArtifact; profile_tree_base_full_artifact's three disclosed-leaf openings are the SAME keyPath/saltHex/value triples as merkleVectors[0] ("size_3_pet_profile_promotion"), and its expected_leaf_hex values match this file's own leafHashVectors/merkleVectors values byte-for-byte - masking never changes a leaf's hash, only whether it is opened or left opaque. Six further isolating negatives (negative_overlap_root_preserving_duplicate_leaf, negative_overlap_reserved_half_matches_disclosed, negative_duplicate_pet_keypath_no_identity_oracle, negative_65_leaves_genuine_root_over_cap, negative_hex32_shape_reserved_missing_0x_prefix, negative_hex32_shape_obfuscated_missing_0x_prefix) were promoted from packages/dogtag-standard-ts/testvectors.json by packages/dogtag-standard-ts/scripts/promote-spec-vectors.ts (WP4.10S P1), which recomputes every disclosed leaf's hash and re-verifies every promoted artifact against the real verifyRedactedArtifact before writing - never hand-copied. Two of the six (the duplicate-keyPath and 64-leaf-cap vectors) use their own distinct keyPath/salt combinations rather than reusing merkleVectors[0]'s three leaves, since isolating those specific checks requires leaves outside that reused set.

leafHashVectors.name: null_leaf
leafHashVectors.notes: TypeTag.Null encodes to zero bytes (encode.ts encodeValue); an absent optional field flattens to this same leaf shape.

leafHashVectors.name: bool_leaf
leafHashVectors.notes: TypeTag.Bool encodes to a single byte: 0x01 for true, 0x00 for false.

leafHashVectors.name: string_leaf
leafHashVectors.notes: TypeTag.String encodes to NFC-normalized UTF-8 bytes.

leafHashVectors.name: string_nfc_leaf
leafHashVectors.notes: NFC case: the input string must already be NFC-normalized before hashing (encode.ts nfc()); a decomposed form (e + combining acute) normalizes to this same precomposed form and MUST hash identically - see nfc_alias_leaf.

leafHashVectors.name: nfc_alias_leaf
leafHashVectors.notes: Byte-distinct input, same NFC normal form as string_nfc_leaf above - MUST produce the identical expected_hex, proving NFC normalization runs before hashing.

leafHashVectors.name: integer_leaf
leafHashVectors.notes: TypeTag.Integer encodes to the canonical decimal-integer ASCII string (no leading zeros, no sign for zero).

leafHashVectors.name: decimal_leaf
leafHashVectors.notes: TypeTag.Decimal encodes the CANONICAL form of the input string: trailing fractional zeros stripped, so this and decimal_leaf_canonical_form_check's raw input differ but MUST hash identically.

leafHashVectors.name: decimal_leaf_canonical_form_check
leafHashVectors.notes: Same keyPath/salt as decimal_leaf, different raw input string, same canonical form - expected_hex MUST equal decimal_leaf's expected_hex.

leafHashVectors.name: bytes_leaf
leafHashVectors.notes: TypeTag.Bytes encodes to the raw bytes unchanged (no NFC, no length prefix at the encodeValue layer). The JSON value here is lowercase hex, no 0x prefix - decode with hexToBytes before hashing.

merkleVectors.name: size_3_pet_profile_promotion
merkleVectors.notes: Odd leaf count (3) exercises odd-promotion: buildMerkle sorts the 3 leaf hashes ascending, hashNode's the first pair, and promotes the third (numerically largest) hash unchanged to the next level, where it is hashNode'd against the first pair's result to form the root. This vector carries the full chain - openings, per-leaf hashes, and the root - so an implementation can be checked at every stage, not just the final root.

merkleVectors.name: size_5_multi_level_fold
merkleVectors.notes: Five leaves - the smallest size at which a per-level re-sort of the fold changes the root (specs/leaf-commitment.md section 7: only the leaf level is ever sorted; every level above it keeps the order the fold produced). `levels` is buildMerkle's own internal layer-by-layer output: levels[0] is the sorted leaf hashes, the last entry is [root_hex]. This tree promotes credentialSubject.name TWICE in a row: once from levels[0] to levels[1] (the leaf-level promotion promoted_leaf_hex/promoted_leaf_keyPath describe below, per this file's existing single-promotion convention from size_3_pet_profile_promotion), and again from levels[1] to levels[2], because levels[1] also has odd length (3) and is never re-sorted before that second fold. levels[1] as the real fold produces it is NOT ascending (species+color's node hash sorts higher than breed+microchip.code's node hash, yet appears first because it was computed first) - an implementation that re-sorted levels[1] before folding would pair a different sibling at levels[2] and reach a different root_hex than the one recorded here.

inclusionVectors.name: size_3_pet_profile_leaf0_inclusion
inclusionVectors.notes: verifyInclusion recomputes hashLeaf(keyPath, salt, scalar) itself, then folds `steps` root-ward; it never trusts a caller-supplied leaf hash.

inclusionVectors.name: size_3_pet_profile_leaf0_tampered_value
inclusionVectors.notes: Same proof and root as the valid vector above, wrong disclosed value - recomputing the leaf yields a different hash, so folding never reaches root_hex.

inclusionVectors.name: size_3_pet_profile_leaf2_species_promote_inclusion
inclusionVectors.notes: Same three-leaf tree as size_3_pet_profile_leaf0_inclusion above, proving inclusion of credentialSubject.species instead of credentialSubject.name. species is the leaf buildMerkle PROMOTES unchanged from level 0 to level 1 (section 7's worked example), so its proof's first step is {promote: true} rather than {sibling} - inclusionVectors[0] and [1] use only {sibling} steps. inclusionVectors[3] also exercises both step shapes, on a taller tree and with two CONSECUTIVE promotions.

inclusionVectors.name: size_5_multi_level_leaf_name_double_promote_inclusion
inclusionVectors.notes: The first proof in this file with more than 2 steps, over the 5-leaf tree (merkleVectors[1] / size_5_multi_level_fold), pinning section 8's one-step-per-tree-level rule on a tree taller than 2 levels. credentialSubject.name is PROMOTED twice in a row: once from levels[0] to levels[1] (it is the unpaired last element of the 5-element level 0), and again from levels[1] to levels[2] (it is again the unpaired last element of the 3-element level 1) - the first two proof steps are therefore both {promote: true}, back to back. The third and final step pairs it against levels[2][0] (already pinned in merkleVectors[1]) to form the root.

redactedArtifactVectors.name: profile_tree_base_full_artifact
redactedArtifactVectors.notes: The same three attribute leaves as merkleVectors[0] ("size_3_pet_profile_promotion"), plus the 3 reserved owner-control hashes every real profile tree carries. Nothing masked: obfuscatedLeafHashes is empty. This is the reference root the masked variants below must reproduce exactly.

redactedArtifactVectors.name: masked_variant_species_obfuscated
redactedArtifactVectors.notes: species moved into obfuscatedLeafHashes. root_hex is IDENTICAL to profile_tree_base_full_artifact's - masking a disclosed leaf never moves R.

redactedArtifactVectors.name: masked_variant_fully_obfuscated
redactedArtifactVectors.notes: Every attribute leaf masked (disclosed: []). Still valid: this artifact format has NO non-maskable attribute keyPath (section 15) - the identity anchor (dogTagIdField) lives outside the tree entirely, never a leaf, so it is never a candidate for masking or omission in the first place.

redactedArtifactVectors.name: negative_overlap
redactedArtifactVectors.notes: species is claimed BOTH disclosed (with its real opening) AND separately obfuscated (with its own genuine hash) - rejected on overlap even though every individual hash is authentic on its own.

redactedArtifactVectors.name: negative_reserved_relabeled_as_obfuscated
redactedArtifactVectors.notes: One of the 3 reserved hashes is moved into obfuscatedLeafHashes instead, leaving only 2 reservedLeafHashes. The naive leaf multiset fed to buildMerkle - and hence the recomputed root - is BIT-IDENTICAL to masked_variant_species_obfuscated's (root_hex matches exactly): only the exactly-3-reserved-hashes count check rejects this. This is the actual non-maskable invariant this artifact format has (section 15) - the reserved triple's count and slot, never an attribute keyPath.

redactedArtifactVectors.name: negative_overlap_root_preserving_duplicate_leaf
redactedArtifactVectors.notes: species's leaf hash is genuinely committed TWICE in this tree (the tree builder enforces keyPath uniqueness only for the 3 reserved leaves, never across ordinary attribute leaves, so two attribute leaves may legitimately fold to the same hash) - one copy is disclosed normally, the other copy's hash is separately listed in obfuscatedLeafHashes. root_hex is the genuine Merkle root over this exact 6-hash multiset (3 reserved + the duplicated species hash + microchip.code), so step 4's root comparison cannot tell this apart from a genuine artifact; only step 3's overlap check, on its obfuscated-half comparison, rejects it.

redactedArtifactVectors.name: negative_overlap_reserved_half_matches_disclosed
redactedArtifactVectors.notes: reservedLeafHashes[0] is deliberately set equal to the disclosed species leaf's own recomputed hash, rather than a genuine owner-control hash (unreachable from a real device tree without a Poseidon preimage - this exercises the verifier's behavior on the wire input directly, not a claim about what a real tree can produce). root_hex is the genuine root over this exact multiset, so only step 3's overlap check, on its reserved-half comparison, rejects it; step 1's exactly-3-reservedLeafHashes count check does not help, since there really are 3 entries.

redactedArtifactVectors.name: negative_duplicate_pet_keypath_no_identity_oracle
redactedArtifactVectors.notes: credentialSubject.name is disclosed TWICE, with different salts, and both openings genuinely fold into root_hex (a device tree has no rule against this for an ordinary attribute keyPath). No expectedIdentityLeaves oracle is supplied, which changes nothing here regardless: credentialSubject.name is not an owner.identity.* keyPath, so that optional cross-check was never going to see it. Since the root recomputes exactly over both openings, only step 2's duplicate-keyPath guard rejects this.

redactedArtifactVectors.name: negative_65_leaves_genuine_root_over_cap
redactedArtifactVectors.notes: 65 total leaf hashes - 3 reserved plus 62 disclosed attribute leaves, one more than the 64-leaf cap (section 10) allows - carrying their own genuine Merkle root over that full multiset, so step 4's root comparison cannot reject it. Only step 1's total-leaf-count check (reservedLeafHashes.length + disclosed.length + obfuscatedLeafHashes.length <= 64) rejects this. The vector is necessarily large: 65 is the smallest leaf count that both exceeds the cap and still carries a self-consistent genuine root, so every one of the 62 attribute leaves has to be listed for root_hex to check out.

redactedArtifactVectors.name: negative_hex32_shape_reserved_missing_0x_prefix
redactedArtifactVectors.notes: reservedLeafHashes[0] is a genuine 64-hex-character field element with its "0x" prefix stripped. It decodes to the identical field element either way (the parser that folds it into the root treats the prefix as optional, stripping it when present), so root_hex is the same genuine root a fully-prefixed posting would produce. Only step 1's hex32-shape check, which requires the literal "0x" prefix, rejects this.

redactedArtifactVectors.name: negative_hex32_shape_obfuscated_missing_0x_prefix
redactedArtifactVectors.notes: obfuscatedLeafHashes[0] (species's hash) is a genuine 64-hex-character field element with its "0x" prefix stripped, decoding to the identical field element either way, so root_hex is the same genuine root a fully-prefixed posting would produce. Only step 1's hex32-shape check, which requires the literal "0x" prefix, rejects this.

recordArtifactVectors.name: record_full_artifact
recordArtifactVectors.notes: The seven non-maskable leaves (specs/leaf-commitment.md section 16) plus two ordinary clinical leaves (vaccineProductName, batchLotNumber), nothing masked: obfuscatedLeafHashes and reservedLeafHashes are both empty. This is the reference root the masked variants below must reproduce exactly.

recordArtifactVectors.name: record_masked_clinical_leaf
recordArtifactVectors.notes: Masks batchLotNumber (a maskable clinical leaf, NOT in the non-maskable set) - moves its hash into obfuscatedLeafHashes and drops its opening from disclosed. Reproduces record_full_artifact's identical root: buildMerkle folds the same 9 leaf hashes either way, so which array names each one is invisible to the root.

recordArtifactVectors.name: record_masked_except_non_maskable
recordArtifactVectors.notes: Masks EVERY clinical leaf (vaccineProductName and batchLotNumber both moved to obfuscatedLeafHashes), disclosing only the seven non-maskable leaves - the falsifiable demonstration that the non-maskable set is real: masking down to exactly this set still verifies (unlike a RedactedTagArtifact, where the non-maskable set is empty and masking down to nothing at all still verifies - specs/leaf-commitment.md section 15). Reproduces record_full_artifact's identical root.

recordArtifactVectors.name: record_negative_masked_dogtagid
recordArtifactVectors.notes: Moves credentialSubject.dogTagId's hash into obfuscatedLeafHashes instead of disclosed - the same 9-hash multiset as record_full_artifact, just repartitioned, so root_hex is bit-identical to it and step 4's root comparison alone cannot reject this. Only the non-maskable-set-must-be-disclosed check (specs/leaf-commitment.md section 16) rejects it, since dogTagId - one of the seven required keyPaths - is no longer found among disclosed's keyPaths.

recordArtifactVectors.name: record_negative_reserved_present
recordArtifactVectors.notes: Carries one entry in reservedLeafHashes (an arbitrary field element, not a genuine owner-control hash - a record artifact never has one to begin with) and FOLDS it into root_hex, so the posted root is the genuine root of this exact 10-hash multiset and the root comparison alone cannot reject it. Every other check passes (all seven non-maskable leaves are disclosed; no overlap). Only the reserved-must-be-empty check rejects this.

recordArtifactVectors.name: record_negative_overlap
recordArtifactVectors.notes: vaccineProductName's leaf hash is genuinely committed TWICE in this tree (a record tree, like a profile tree, enforces no cross-leaf uniqueness among ordinary attribute leaves) - one copy is disclosed normally, the other copy's hash is separately listed in obfuscatedLeafHashes. root_hex is the genuine Merkle root over this exact 9-hash multiset (7 non-maskable plus the duplicated vaccineProductName hash twice), so the root comparison cannot tell this apart from a genuine artifact; only the overlap check rejects it.
